subject: AI & Agents
title: Self-Attention Step by Step
description: Learn Self-Attention Step by Step in one minute.

hook.text: Every word in a sentence asks three questions: What am I? What do I want? What can I offer?

buildup.text: Each token produces three vectors: Query (what I seek), Key (what I offer), Value (my content).

discovery.text: Queries match against Keys to produce attention scores. High scores mean strong relevance.

twist.text: The model doesn't pick one word to attend to — it blends all words, weighted by relevance.

climax.text: The result: each word gets a context-rich representation that incorporates the entire sentence.

punchline.text: Ask, match, blend. That's attention in three steps.

quiz.question: What are the three vectors in self-attention?

details.summary: Self-attention lets each word in a sentence look at every other word to determine which are most relevant to its meaning. Each word computes a weighted sum of all words, with weights reflecting relevance.
details.whyItMatters: Self-attention is the core mechanism behind Transformer models. It enables contextual understanding — the same word gets different representations depending on surrounding words.
takeaways: Each word attends to every other word in the input sequence
Attention weights indicate which words are most relevant to each other

faq.question: How does self-attention compute word relationships?
faq.answer: Each word is projected into query, key, and value vectors. The query of one word is matched against keys of all words to compute attention scores. These scores weight the values to produce a context-aware representation.

faq.question: Why is self-attention better than previous approaches?
faq.answer: Unlike RNNs that lose information over long distances, self-attention directly connects every word pair. A word at position 1 can attend to position 1000 just as easily, enabling superior long-range understanding.
